title: Equivalences preserve strict section spaces of right fibrations
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, functor equivalences, internal functor simplicial sets and Kan complexes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and right fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $A,B$ be small quasicategories in a fixed universe, $e:A\to B$ a functor equivalence, and $q:E\to B$ a right fibration of small simplicial sets. For $a:K\to B$, define the simplicial set $\Gamma_a(q)$ by
$$\Gamma_a(q)_n=\{h:K\times\Delta^n\to E\mid qh=a\operatorname{pr}_K\},$$
with simplicial operators given by precomposition on the $\Delta^n$ factor. Then $\Gamma_{\mathrm{id}_B}(q)$ and $\Gamma_e(q)$ are Kan complexes, and precomposition induces a simplicial homotopy equivalence
$$e^*:\Gamma_{\mathrm{id}_B}(q)\longrightarrow\Gamma_e(q),\qquad h\longmapsto h(e\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^n}).$$
Here simplicial homotopy equivalence means that a simplicial map $c$ in the other direction exists, with simplicial homotopies from $ce^*$ and $e^*c$ to the respective identities, modeled by product with $\Delta^1$; either endpoint orientation is allowed. No nonemptiness assumption on these section spaces is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.1.13 (02NC), right-cofinal assertion, unpacked with Definition 7.2.1.1. Corollary 4.4.2.5 (01GZ) gives the two Kan complexes. These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED.

proof.text: First $E$ is a quasicategory: project any inner horn to $B$, fill it there, and lift the resulting simplex against the same inner horn using the right-fibration hypothesis. Opposite simplicial sets reverse faces and degeneracies and take $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$, so $q^{\mathrm{op}}:E^{\mathrm{op}}\to B^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a left fibration between small quasicategories. Apply [lem-cbc-left-fibration-equivalence-lift]. Its reflection clause, on taking opposites, says that $q$ reflects equivalence edges. Its prescribed-target lifting clause, applied to the opposite of an equivalence $q(x)\to b$, gives an equivalence in $E$ with prescribed source $x$ over that edge. Thus $q$ lifts inner horns and equivalences with prescribed source: it is an isofibration. Reversing the two inverse-triangle witnesses in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] justifies every use of opposites here.

source.place: Example 4.4.1.11 and Proposition 4.4.2.11 (019K): right fibrations are conservative isofibrations These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; online text read, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $K=A,B$, put $\mathcal D_K=\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$, $\mathcal C_K=\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)$ and let $p_K:\mathcal D_K\to\mathcal C_K$ be postcomposition with $q$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to $q$ and the empty inclusion $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$. Since a functor simplicial set out of the empty set is a point, its exponential corner is exactly $p_K$; both its source and target are quasicategories and $p_K$ is an isofibration. By [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration], $r_K=p_K^\simeq:\mathcal D_K^\simeq\to\mathcal C_K^\simeq$ is a Kan fibration. Both cores are Kan: apply the same core-fibration statement to each quasicategory's map to a point, an isofibration since its only required equivalence lift is a degenerate edge. All these functor simplicial sets remain small in the fixed universe.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.1 and Proposition 4.4.3.7 (01EZ), specialized to empty-domain exponentiation These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; online text read, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $a:K\to B$ and $K=A,B$, the strict fiber of $p_K$ over the vertex $a$ has $n$-simplices exactly the maps $h:K\times\Delta^n\to E$ satisfying $qh=a\operatorname{pr}_K$, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Every edge $\tau$ of this fiber has, at each vertex $k$ of $K$, a component in $E$ whose image under $q$ is the degenerate edge at $a(k)$. The reflection assertion of Step 1 makes this component an equivalence. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences], $\tau$ is an equivalence in $\mathcal D_K$. Consequently every simplex of the strict fiber lies in $\mathcal D_K^\simeq$, and the strict fibers of $p_K$ and $r_K$ over $a$ are equal as simplicial sets, not merely equivalent. They are precisely $\Gamma_a(q)$. A horn in a fiber of the Kan fibration $r_K$ fills over the constant simplex at $a$, so $\Gamma_a(q)$ is Kan. This proves the two Kan assertions for $a=\mathrm{id}_B$ and $a=e$.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.2.5, with Theorem 4.4.4.4 (01DK): strict sections are the core fibers These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; online text read, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose a simplicial quasi-inverse $d:B\to A$ and coherent natural equivalences $de\simeq\mathrm{id}_A$ and $ed\simeq\mathrm{id}_B$ from the functor-equivalence hypothesis. For $C=E,B$, let $R_C$ be restriction along $e$ and $D_C$ restriction along $d$.

source.place: Functor-equivalence definition and coherent natural equivalences; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: The coherent equivalence $ed\simeq\mathrm{id}_B$ supplies the whiskering cylinder between $D_CR_C$ and $\mathrm{id}$, and the analogous equivalence on $A$ supplies the cylinder between $R_CD_C$ and $\mathrm{id}$, by [lem-coef-infinity-precomposition-cylinder].

source.place: Proposition 3.1.7.13 forward implication; Kerodon source archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: These cylinders restrict to the cores by [lem-coef-infinity-core-cylinder-restriction]. Its hypotheses hold because the components of the chosen coherent natural equivalences are equivalence edges, and the pointwise criterion identifies equivalences in each internal functor simplicial set.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4 and the edge-and-triangle calculation; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Thus $D_CR_C$ and $R_CD_C$ are simplicially homotopic to the respective identities on cores. Applying [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] shows that both $R_E$ and $R_B$ are weak homotopy equivalences. Either endpoint orientation is permitted.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.7.13 forward implication; Kerodon source archival copy WANTED.

proof.text:
There is a strictly commutative square of Kan complexes with top map $R_E:\mathcal D_B^\simeq\to\mathcal D_A^\simeq$, bottom map $R_B:\mathcal C_B^\simeq\to\mathcal C_A^\simeq$, and vertical maps $r_B,r_A$. Its commutativity is the equality $q\circ(F\circ e)=(q\circ F)\circ e$ in every simplicial degree. Both horizontal maps are weak homotopy equivalences by Step 7, and $R_B$ takes the vertex $\mathrm{id}_B$ to the vertex $e$. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] to this square, with its constant commutativity homotopy. The forward direction of its equivalence yields a weak homotopy equivalence
$$\phi:\operatorname{hofib}_{\mathrm{id}_B}(r_B)\longrightarrow\operatorname{hofib}_e(r_A).$$
In the path-space models its map is exactly $(x,\gamma)\mapsto(R_E(x),R_B\circ\gamma)$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.7.1, in the existing homotopy-fiber formulation These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; online text read, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] to each pair $r_B,\{\mathrm{id}_B\}\to\mathcal C_B^\simeq$ and $r_A,\{e\}\to\mathcal C_A^\simeq$. Its hypotheses hold because the bases and total spaces are Kan and $r_B,r_A$ are Kan fibrations. Using Step 3, it gives weak homotopy equivalences $j_B:\Gamma_{\mathrm{id}_B}(q)\to\operatorname{hofib}_{\mathrm{id}_B}(r_B)$ and $j_A:\Gamma_e(q)\to\operatorname{hofib}_e(r_A)$, both inserting constant paths. They satisfy $j_Ae^*=\phi j_B$ exactly: precomposition takes the family $h$ to $h(e\times\mathrm{id})$ and takes its constant base path to the constant path at $e$. The right-hand composite and $j_A$ induce bijections on components and isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups; cancelling those of $j_A$ shows that the specified $e^*$ does as well. Hence $e^*$ is a weak homotopy equivalence of the two strict section Kan complexes.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.7: natural constant-path comparison of strict fibers with path-space homotopy fibers These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; online text read, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Now [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse] applies directly to $e^*$: Step 3 proved its source and target Kan, and Step 9 proved precisely the realized component and based-homotopy-group conditions in that node's statement. It gives a simplicial map $c:\Gamma_e(q)\to\Gamma_{\mathrm{id}_B}(q)$ and homotopies on product with $\Delta^1$ from $ce^*$ and $e^*c$ to the respective identities. This is the claimed simplicial homotopy equivalence. The theorem explicitly permits empty Kan complexes. Every earlier fiber comparison also permits empty fibers, so the argument has made no nonemptiness assumption.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.7.13, converse for Kan complexes; realization convention as in Corollary 3.6.4.3 (03X7) These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; online text read, archival copy WANTED.
